subject: EdgeHealth: proposal for customer-specific log retention & evidence path
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@edgehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: legal@edgehealth.com
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: EdgeHealth retention ask: 12-month logs for clinical audit

Hi Karthik —

Quick question from our compliance team: EdgeHealth needs application and access logs retained for 12 months for upcoming clinical audits. We understand Redwood's default customer log TTL is 30 days for production inference logs. Can you confirm whether a customer-specific exception is possible, what controls are required for SOC 2 / SIG evidence, and whether there are any service or cost impacts?

Specific asks:
- Can Redwood retain the following logs for 12 months for EdgeHealth only? (application_request_logs, inference_activity, auth_audit)
- What evidence would you provide to satisfy SOC 2 (e.g., retained log exports, access controls, WORM) and SIG/CAIQ questions?
- Any timeline or procurement/legal changes needed (amendment/DocuSign)?

We are preparing to respond to an upcoming audit window in early June and would appreciate a written proposal and next steps.

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Compliance, EdgeHealth
Alicia.Gomez@edgehealth.com

[Attachment: edgehealth_log_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Team — forwarding EdgeHealth's ask. TL;DR: they want a customer-specific 12-month retention for three log classes. Need a pragmatic proposal that: (1) preserves their data for 12 months, (2) produces SOC 2/SIG evidence they can hand auditors, and (3) outlines cost/operational impact and any legal amendment required.

Can each of you weigh in on:

- Stephanie: what the minimum controls/evidence bundle should include for SOC 2 + SIG (retention confirmation, role-based access logs, export manifests, tamper-evidence).
- Neha: legal/process — is DocuSign amendment + PO sufficient? Any redlines we should flag?

I put a hard internal target to have an outbound proposal to Alicia by EOD. If we cannot meet that, let's aim for tomorrow morning but include a clear timeline.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: EdgeHealth retention ask: 12-month logs for clinical audit

Karthik / team — notes from infra:

Summary of options (rough):
1) Per-tenant long-term bucket (preferred):
   - Route identified log classes to an EdgeHealth-dedicated S3/GCS bucket with lifecycle rules set to 12 months then delete.
   - Apply bucket-level IAM + object versioning; enable server-side encryption (KMS) with a customer-managed key option (if requested).
   - Pros: minimal changes to runtime, low retrieval latency for evidence exports.
   - Cons: additional storage costs; snapshot/ingest pipeline must be tested for throughput.

2) Periodic export to immutable archive (log escrow):
   - Daily export of consolidated logs to WORM-compliant archive (third-party escrow) for 12 months.
   - Pros: stronger tamper-evidence; isolation from production.
   - Cons: operational complexity, integration timeline longer (~3-6 weeks).

3) Extended retention in hot cluster (not recommended):
   - Keep logs in primary hot retention for 12 months — expensive and not necessary for most audit needs.

Preliminary cost impact: estimate ~150–300 GB/mo depending on traffic pattern (EdgeHealth is mid-volume). Ballpark incremental storage $0.02–0.05 per GB/mo; we should run exact calc after sampling.

Technical caveats:
- We need to ensure PII/PHI handling aligns with their DPA. If they require customer-managed KMS, we will need a short integration (~1 week).
- For SOC 2, we can provide export manifests and storage access logs; for tamper evidence recommend WORM or object versioning + retention.

I've attached a draft architecture note and a CSV with retention-option cost scenarios.

Attachments: [retention_options.csv], [kb-log-architecture.pdf]

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Infra Ops Lead, Redwood Inference

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: EdgeHealth retention ask: 12-month logs for clinical audit

Thanks Marissa — compliance view:

Minimum evidence bundle to satisfy typical SOC 2 auditor expectations for a retention exception:
- Written amendment signed by both parties that defines the specific log classes, retention period (12 months), and deletion procedure. (DocuSign)
- Exportable retention manifest showing object timestamps, hashes, and retention-policy metadata for the 12-month window.
- Access control evidence: RBAC mapping and access logs for the long-term bucket (who accessed exports, admin ops).
- Proof of encryption and KMS usage; if customer-managed KMS is enabled, include key management logs.
- Process description for deletion with screenshots or runbook excerpt and a dry-run deletion report.

SIG/CAIQ mapping: we can map each item above to the appropriate CAIQ questions (logging, cryptography, retention). I recommend we pre-build the mapping doc so EdgeHealth can include it in their SIG.

Operational constraints:
- If we choose the per-tenant bucket route, we can generate the evidence within 2–3 business days after exports are enabled.
- If they require escrow/WORM, plan 3–4 weeks for integration testing.

I'll draft the amendment language for neha to review (I can reuse our standard retention amendment template and add a clause for log classes).

-Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Hi Alicia —

Thanks for the clear ask. Internal consensus (summary + proposal):

Proposal (recommended, minimal disruption):
- Route the requested log classes (application_request_logs, inference_activity, auth_audit) to an EdgeHealth-dedicated long-term object store (S3/GCS) with a 12-month lifecycle.
- Enable object versioning and server-side encryption; offer customer-managed KMS as an option (you told us previously you prefer us to host keys but will confirm).
- We will generate an evidence bundle including: retention manifests (timestamps + hashes), bucket access logs, KMS usage logs (if enabled), and a deletion runbook + dry-run report. We will also produce a SIG mapping doc.

Operational impact & timeline:
- If EdgeHealth accepts the per-tenant bucket option, we can enable exports within 3–5 business days after procurement sign-off and completion of any requested KMS setup.
- Escrow/WORM option is available but requires ~3–4 weeks (additional integration testing and vendor onboarding).
- Estimated incremental storage cost: ballpark $0.02–0.05/GB/mo; we will share a precise estimate after you confirm traffic/sample window.

Legal/procurement:
- We will provide an amendment draft to be signed via DocuSign that specifies the log classes, retention duration, encryption options, and deletion procedure. Neha, Stephanie — this is the action item for drafting and review.

Next steps for EdgeHealth:
1) Confirm preferred retention method (per-tenant bucket vs escrow).
2) Confirm whether you need customer-managed KMS.
3) Confirm PO or amendment signoff timeline — we can begin technical enablement once we have that.

I've attached an amendment draft (ETA EOD tomorrow) and the cost/capacity CSV.

Attachments: [EdgeHealth-retention-amendment-draft.docx], [retention_options.csv]

Best,
Karthik
